summary: Attacked the extraction of Nikolaus–Scholze, 'On topological cyclic homology' (Acta Math. 221 (2018) 203–409, with the correction in Acta Math. 222 (2019) 215–218; arXiv 1707.01799v2 is the last preprint). The extraction has 162 items, 6 routes and 25 source issues, and the review accepted it. The source hashes reproduce. The main theorems, the routing and the 0-library status hold, and E1 (Proposition II.3.4's fibre-product identification is false; KU counterexample) re-derives. There are eleven findings: five medium, six low, none high. (1) Items /68–/70 and /74 write R_F for R_{F̄}, so /70 states the lemma's hypothesis as its conclusion and drops 'F preserves pullbacks'. (2) /60 misstates Goodwillie's integral TC^gen: it is a pullback over primes (p. 266), and the p-completion facts TC(X)_p^∧ ≃ TC(X_p^∧, p) used in §IV.3 have no item. (3) Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5 (item /124) are stated for p-cyclotomic spectra but need a T-action. The paper's claim that the action 'extends automatically' contradicts its own Remark II.1.3; this is a new source error. (4) Trivial cyclotomic spectra (/136, /137) are also owned by the RefinedTraceMethods Part II through the accepted Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction. (5) The ∞-category Sp, bounded below spectra, p-completion and Postnikov truncations have no items or statuses. Low: /138's inputs (footnote 9, Mahowald–Hopkins); hypotheses of /104, /55 and /155; five unrecorded misprints; the review's wrong amendment of E22 (the correction does list pp. 281 and 284); review route reasons that do not match the routes; no per-issue review verdicts and no sourceVersions.
checked: Independence. The extraction PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18 was written by cc-442dc5 (issue #2192, commit 9ea79d87), and REV-PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18 by cc-7b31c4 (issue #2193, commit 11da90fc). cc-f805bf appears in none of the four target files (.result.json, .md, .review.json, reviews/REV-PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18.md). This session wrote and reviewed none of the other extractions or packets cited here.

The source, fetched 30 September 2026. The open-access Acta PDF (https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/acta/2018/0221/0002/ACTA-2018-0221-0002-a001.pdf, 207 pages, created 31 March 2019) has SHA-256 8b1856fa8faefa3efebd64580249aa6fbc0c918f69820bba01410ab0ef1eb8ef. The Acta correction (Acta Math. 222 (2019) 215–218) has 0b98fb63029a31324ad23504f584e3f414b03f4734ba63f49b943b0bd5f27944. arXiv v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.01799v2) has 12b6cdbd0d8ebb506284bd13f183affe80e41cc8890fef5fa21c922c2f80cec3. All three match the recorded hashes. The arXiv abstract page lists only v1 (6 July 2017) and v2 (7 September 2018). No correction to the paper was found beyond the Acta correction.

The whole paper was re-read in the text layer: the introduction and Chapters I, II, III, IV and Appendices A–C with the references, in parallel parts. Every finding filed here was checked personally against the text. Page images at 150–300 dpi were checked for pp. 219, 220, 224, 238, 253, 254, 259, 270, 271, 276, 288, 293, 310, 332, 365, 373, 377, 378, 387, 389, 394 and 399.

Coverage. All 263 numbered statements the text layer yields were compared with the 162 items, their locators and their notes. Only remarks, Constructions III.6.3–III.6.4 (covered by the /106 statement), Example A.11 and Remark B.8 are not named. None of these is used later except as reported in findings 2 and 6. The named examples in the job were all checked: stable ∞-categories (/4), the Tate construction (/10), the Tate diagonal (/85, /94), the Segal conjecture and Lin/Gunawardena (/86, /88), genuine and Borel G-spectra (/42–/51), cyclotomic spectra in both senses (/34, /38, /52–/55), THH as a cyclotomic spectrum (/92, /93), TC = map(S, THH) (/40), the bounded below equivalence (/82), Frobenius lifts (/124), spherical Witt vectors (/110) and TC(F_p) (/133). The paper never computes TC of perfect F_p-algebras other than F_p. The ∞-category Sp itself has no item (finding 5).
Every item's statement and locator for /1–/162 was checked (number and printed page). Beyond the findings, all locators hold, including Lemma B.7 on p. 386 before Construction B.9 on p. 387.

Source issues. E1 was re-derived: fibres ∏_pΩ^∞W_p^{hT} against ∏_pΩ^∞W_p^{hC_{p^∞}}, with W_p^{hC_{p^∞}} ≃ W_p because H^s(C_{p^∞}; V) = 0 for s > 0 and rational V; the Gysin fibre Σ^{−2}W_p^{hT}; W_p ≠ 0. No later stated result relies on the false identification, since §II.6 uses the coalgebra functor. E2 (the half-open cover of Δ/T and its repair by closed intervals), E3 (the HZ → HQ counterexample, using that TC of a connective cyclotomic spectrum is (−2)-connective), E4, E5 (degrees 2n(p−1) of the F_p^×-invariant classes t^{n(p−1)}, |t| = −2) and E6–E19 are confirmed. E20, E21, E23, E24 and E25 were checked against the correction's list. E22 is wrong as amended (finding 9).

findings.claim: Four items write R_F where the paper has R_{F̄}, the right adjoint of the shifted-coalgebra functor F̄: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F, which is a different functor from R_F: C → C, the right adjoint of F. In /70 (Lemma II.5.4) this makes the item false as a summary of the lemma. It states the conclusion as 'the counit F R_F → id is an equivalence', which is the standing hypothesis of the lemma (R_F fully faithful). The lemma's actual conclusion, that the counit F̄R_{F̄} → id is an equivalence, is lost. /70 also omits two hypotheses the lemma and Corollary II.5.5 use: C presentable with F colimit-preserving (Construction II.5.2), and F preserves pullbacks. In /68, /69 and /74 the same substitution turns the coreflection formula ιR_ι = lim(… → R_{F̄}² → R_{F̄} → id) into a limit of endofunctors of C. These items carry the proofs of Theorem II.5.6 (p. 272: 'We see from Lemma II.5.4 that Φ̄^{C_p}R_{C_p} ≃ id', then Proposition II.5.3) and Lemma II.5.11 (p. 276, via Corollary II.5.5), and through them Theorems II.5.13, II.6.3 and II.6.9.
findings.evidence: Page image of p. 270 (published text, PDF p. 68): 'Now, we give a formula for the functor R_{F̄}: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F, which was by definition the right adjoint of the functor F̄: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F from Construction II.5.2. … Denote this right adjoint by R_F: C → C. We assume that the counit of the adjunction FR_F → id_C be a natural equivalence. … We moreover assume that F preserves pullbacks. Lemma II.5.4. The functor R_{F̄}: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F takes a coalgebra X → FX to the coalgebra R_{F̄}(X → FX) = Y → FY … Moreover, the counit F̄R_{F̄} → id is an equivalence.' The same page displays '… → R³_{F̄}X → R²_{F̄}X → R_{F̄}X → X' for Proposition II.5.3. Page image of p. 276 has R_{F̄_n} in Lemmas II.5.10–II.5.11. The text layer drops the bars, which is probably how the error arose. Item /70 reads 'If F has a fully faithful right adjoint R_F (unit η), R_F sends a coalgebra φ: X → FX to Y = X ×_{R_F F X} R_F X … the counit F R_F → id is an equivalence.'
findings.fix: In /68, /69 and /74 replace R_F (and R_{F_n}) by R_{F̄} (R_{F̄_n}) wherever the right adjoint of F̄ on CoAlg_F is meant. Restate /70 as: 'Let C be presentable and F: C → C colimit-preserving and pullback-preserving, with right adjoint R_F: C → C such that the counit F R_F → id is an equivalence (unit η). Then R_{F̄}: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F sends φ: X → FX to Y = X ×_{R_F F X} R_F X (along η_X and R_Fφ), with structure map Y → X ≃ F R_F X ≃ FY, and the counit F̄R_{F̄} → id is an equivalence; R_{F̄}^k X is the iterated fibre product (Corollary II.5.5).'

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18.result.json: item PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/60; also /66 and /124 (inputs they use that no item states)
findings.claim: Item /60 says that integral genuine TC 'is defined by diagram (1) over all n', with locator Definition II.4.4, p. 263. Diagram (1) is on p. 266, not in Definition II.4.4. It is Goodwillie's definition, a pullback over primes: TC^gen(X) = X^{hT} ×_{∏_p (X_p^∧)^{hT}} ∏_p TC^gen(X, p)_p^∧. It is not a limit over n. Two facts that the paper proves in §II.4 and uses later have no item. (a) In (1) both vertical maps are profinite completions, because (X_p^∧)^{hT} ≃ (X_p^∧)^{hC_{p^∞}}; the proof of Theorem II.4.11 uses this. (b) For bounded below X, TC(X)_p^∧ ≃ TC(X_p^∧) ≃ TC(X_p^∧, p); Proposition IV.3.4 (item /124) cites this.
findings.evidence: Published text p. 266: 'Recall from [32, Lemma 6.4.3.2] Goodwillie's definition of the integral topological cyclic homology for a genuine cyclotomic spectrum X in the sense of Definition II.3.3. It is defined by the pullback square TC^gen(X) → X^{hT} over ∏_{p∈P} TC^gen(X, p)_p^∧ → ∏_{p∈P} (X_p^∧)^{hT} (1). … It follows that the right vertical map is a profinite completion, and therefore also the left vertical map is a profinite completion.' Published text pp. 351–352: 'Recall that if X is a p-cyclotomic spectrum which is bounded below, then TC(X)_p^∧ = TC(X_p^∧) = TC(X_p^∧, p). In order words, the p-completion of TC(X) can be computed in terms of X_p^∧ as either TC(X_p^∧) or TC(X_p^∧, p); this follows from the discussion in §II.4.' The proof of Proposition IV.3.4 then uses 'As TC(X) = TC(X, p)'. No item statement contains either fact (searched all 162 statements and notes); /59 (Lemma II.4.2) gives only the profinite completion of X^{tT}.
findings.fix: In /60 replace the last clause by: 'For genuine cyclotomic X, TC^gen(X) is defined (Goodwillie, [32, Lemma 6.4.3.2]) by the pullback (1), p. 266: TC^gen(X) = X^{hT} ×_{∏_p (X_p^∧)^{hT}} ∏_p TC^gen(X, p)_p^∧', and add 'p. 266' to its locator. Add an item 'p-completion of TC' (§II.4, p. 266, and p. 351): (a) both vertical maps in (1) are profinite completions; (b) for bounded below cyclotomic X, TC(X)_p^∧ ≃ TC(X_p^∧) ≃ TC(X_p^∧, p). Status missing, routed with route 1 to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.2. KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.4/integral-and-p-typical-tc-agree-after-completion plans the Hesselholt–Madsen form and should cite it.

findings.claim: Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5 are stated for p-cyclotomic spectra. By Definition II.1.1(ii) these carry only a C_{p^∞}-action, and a Frobenius lift is defined as C_{p^∞}-equivariant. The statements and proofs, however, use X^{hT}, ΣX_{hT} and a T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant lift. The paper covers this with 'in this case the C_{p^∞}-action on X_p^∧ extends automatically to a T-action', which its own Remark II.1.3 contradicts. A counterexample: X = HF_p[C_{p^∞}] with the translation action and φ_p = 0 (so φ̃_p = 0 is a Frobenius lift). It is bounded below and p-complete, being an HF_p-module, but C_{p^∞} acts non-trivially on π_0 = F_p[C_{p^∞}]. The action therefore does not extend to the connected group T, which acts trivially on homotopy. The results are correct for cyclotomic spectra, i.e. with a T-action and a T-equivariant lift. The application, Theorem IV.3.6 on Σ^∞_+LY, has one. Item /124 copies the p-cyclotomic hypothesis ('a bounded below p-complete p-cyclotomic X with a C_{p^∞}-equivariant Frobenius lift … TC(X) is the pullback of ΣX_{hT} → X'). As written, the item is not well formed. No sourceIssue records the mistake.
findings.evidence: Published text p. 351: 'we say that a Frobenius lift on a p-cyclotomic spectrum (X, φ_p) is a C_{p^∞}-equivariant factorization of the morphism φ_p: X → X^{tC_p} as the composite of a map φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p} and the projection'. P. 352: 'Note also that in this case the C_{p^∞}-action on X_p^∧ extends automatically to a T-action. Proposition IV.3.4. For a bounded below p-complete p-cyclotomic spectrum X with a Frobenius lift φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p}, we obtain a pullback square' with ΣX_{hT}. The proof of Lemma IV.3.5 (p. 353) begins: 'Note that the T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant map φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p} is equivalently given by a natural transformation ψ_p of functors BT → Sp'. Remark II.1.3, p. 241: 'However, not every C_{p^∞}-action on a p-complete spectrum extends to a T-action, since a C_{p^∞}-action can act non-trivially on homotopy groups.' The same text is in arXiv v2, and the Acta correction does not mention it.
findings.fix: Restate /124 for a bounded below p-complete cyclotomic spectrum X (a spectrum with T-action and T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant φ_p), with a T-equivariant Frobenius lift φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p}, and TC(X, p) ≃ TC(X) for such X. Add sourceIssue PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E26: kind error, affects 'a stated result' (Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5 as stated), locator 'p. 351 (definition of Frobenius lift), p. 352 (Proposition IV.3.4), p. 353 (Lemma IV.3.5); also arXiv v2', correction 'assume a T-action and a T-equivariant lift', reason as above with the HF_p[C_{p^∞}] example, known 'new'.

No item covers any of these, so none has a status. Many items and the brief of route 6 are stated in terms of them: /12, /21 and /88 use bounded below and p-completion, /16 and /18 use Postnikov pieces, and /84 and /97 use the symmetric monoidal structure of Sp. PROTOCOL §0 and §16 require an item, with its status, for every definition the paper uses. These notions are not uniformly planned. findings.claim: Item /138 (TC of E_2-rings of characteristic p, with the fibre sequence 'even without bounded below') depends on two inputs that have no item. (a) Footnote (9) of §I.2: the Tate orbit and Tate fixpoint lemmas hold for all HZ-module spectra (chain complexes), with no boundedness hypothesis. /12 assumes bounded below, and /19 covers only Eilenberg–MacLane spectra HM. The unbounded case is exactly what /138 uses. (b) The Mahowald–Hopkins theorem (Remark IV.4.5, p. 357): HF_p is the free E_2-algebra in Sp with a chosen nullhomotopy of p. The paper uses it to make A an algebra over HF_p. Only the note of /130 mentions it. The paper's phrase 'E_2-HF_p-algebra' also overstates what this gives, namely an E_2-map HF_p → A. That map suffices for THH(A) to be a THH(HF_p)-module in cyclotomic spectra, and /138 repeats the phrase.
findings.evidence: Published text p. 219, footnote (9): 'One can, however, check that they hold for all chain complexes, as then both (X_{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} and (X^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} are modules over the E_∞-ring spectrum (HZ^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)} ≃ 0.' P. 357, Remark IV.4.5: 'there is a short argument, given in [16] and [17], deducing it from the following theorem of Mahowald–Hopkins. (i) The free E_2-algebra in Sp with a chosen nullhomotopy p=0 is given by HF_p.' Pp. 364–365: 'Fixing a nullhomotopy from p to 0, we get that A is an E_2-HF_p-algebra, by Remark IV.4.5. … This implies that there is a fiber sequence TC(A) → THH(A)^{hT} → THH(A)^{tT}, even if A is not bounded below, as, for HZ-module spectra, the Tate orbit lemma is always valid.'

Add item 'Mahowald–Hopkins: HF_p is the free E_2-algebra in Sp with a nullhomotopy of p (cited)' (Remark IV.4.5, p. 357), missing, routed with /138. In /138 write 'an E_2-ring map HF_p → A (Mahowald–Hopkins)' for 'E_2-HF_p-algebra'. Add [16]/[17] (the references Remark IV.4.5 gives for the Mahowald–Hopkins argument) to the prerequisites if the atlas does not cover them.

findings.claim: Three item statements are imprecise. (a) /104 states that the maps Φ_p on classical THH(R) are F-equivalences for every orthogonal ring spectrum R. The paper's argument passes from degreewise equivalences to the naive realisation. That step needs the cyclic spaces to be proper, which the paper proves only under Lemma III.5.2's hypotheses (R levelwise well pointed, S⁰ → R_0 an h-cofibration). Remark III.5.3 says the paper will not prove more. (b) /55's coherence identity has mismatched sources. Its left side starts from Φ^{C_m}_U Φ^{C_n}_U X, while Φ_n ∘ Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ_m) starts from Φ^{C_n}_U Φ^{C_m}_U X, which is the paper's order. (c) /155 copies the misprint in Proposition B.19(ii): 'proper paracyclic' should be 'proper cyclic', since sd_p^* is only defined on cyclic objects and a paracyclic realisation carries only an R-action, not a T-action.
findings.evidence: Published text p. 312, Lemma III.5.2: 'Assume that the orthogonal ring spectrum R is levelwise well pointed and that the unit in the zeroth space S⁰ → R_0 is an h-cofibration. Then, the cyclic spaces THH(R; X): Λ^op → Top are proper'; preceded by 'According to Corollary B.16, we have to verify that THH(R; X) is proper'. P. 315: 'By Proposition III.5.5 and Theorem III.4.7, the maps Φ_p are equivalences of the underlying orthogonal spectra.' P. 259, Definition II.3.6, with the identification Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ^{C_m}_U X) ≃ Φ^{C_{mn}}_U X. P. 394: 'Using the functor sd_p: Λ_p → Λ, we get for every cyclic object X a subdivided Λ_p-object sd_p^*X'; p. 395, Proposition B.19(ii): 'For a proper paracyclic topological space (resp. spectrum) X, there is a natural T-equivariant homeomorphism |X| ≅ |sd_p^*X|'.
findings.fix: (a) Add to /104 the hypothesis 'R levelwise well pointed with S⁰ → R_0 an h-cofibration (Lemma III.5.2)', or a note that §III.5 assumes it. (b) In /55 write Φ_{mn} ∘ (Φ^{C_n}_U Φ^{C_m}_U X ≃ Φ^{C_{mn}}_U X) = Φ_n ∘ Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ_m). (c) In /155 write 'proper cyclic', and record the misprint (finding 8).

findings.claim: Five mistakes in the paper are not recorded. All are in the published text and in arXiv v2, and the Acta correction lists none of them. (1) Proof of Corollary I.4.3, p. 238: it cites 'Lemma I.2.6 (ii)' for commuting with Postnikov limits lim τ_{≤n}, which is part (i); part (ii) is about colimits over τ_{≥−n}. (2) Proof of Theorem III.4.7, p. 310: 'n_V = min_{H⊊V}(…)' and 'for varying H⊊V' should read H ⊊ C_p. H runs over subgroups of C_p (the case split is H = C_p versus H ⊊ C_p), and V is a representation. (3) Proposition B.19(ii), p. 395: 'proper paracyclic' should be 'proper cyclic' (see finding 7(c)). (4) Footnote (46), p. 389: 'f(0) is the successor of min t^{-1}(R≥0)' should be 'predecessor'. The text defines f(1/(n+1)) = min t^{-1}(R≥0) and f(k/(n+1)) as the successor of f((k−1)/(n+1)) for k = 1, …, n, so f(1/(n+1)) is the successor of f(0). Read literally, the footnote makes f(0) > f(1/(n+1)), and f is not non-decreasing. (5) Proof of Proposition A.14, p. 378: 'a transformation G′_1F → G′_0' is reversed. The 2-cell set up on p. 377 is G_0 → G_1∘LF, and a functor out of the mapping cylinder M(φ) gives G′_0 → G′_1F.
findings.evidence: Page image of p. 310 (PDF p. 108): 'n_V = min_{H⊊V}(n+dim V^H − dim ϱ^H_{C_p}|S̄|m) denote the minimum of these numbers for varying H⊊V'; arXiv v2 p. 88 has the same. P. 238: 'commutes with Postnikov limits as in Lemma I.2.6 (ii). Thus, by taking the limit over all τ_{≤n}X'; Lemma I.2.6 (p. 222): '(i) The natural maps Y^{hG} → lim_n(τ_{≤n}Y)^{hG} … (ii) The natural maps colim_n(τ_{≥−n}Y)_{hG} → Y_{hG} …'. P. 389: 'with f(1/(n+1)) = min t^{-1}(R≥0) … and f(k/(n+1)) is the successor of f((k−1)/(n+1)) for 1 ⩽ k ⩽ n.(46)' and footnote (46): 'Note that k=1 is also included, so that f(0) is the successor of min t^{-1}(R≥0).' Pp. 377–378: 'with a not-necessarily invertible 2-cell … G_0 → G_1 ∘ LF' and 'a functor G′_1: X_1 → D which sends W to equivalences and a transformation G′_1F → G′_0'. Pp. 394–395 as quoted in finding 7.
findings.fix: Add sourceIssues PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18/E27–E31, each kind misprint, affects nothing, known new. Searched: the Acta correction, arXiv v1 and v2.

findings.claim: The review's route reasons do not describe the routes it accepted. Route 1: '22 planned items listed alongside', but route 1 lists 15; the 23 are spread over routes 1, 3, 4 and 5. Route 2: 'the cyclic bar construction for an ordinary ring and the HKR comparison the paper cites', but route 2 carries the HKR filtration (/127) and HH(F_p) (/129). Route 3: 'lax equalizers, coalgebras for endofunctors and their coreflection', but those (/36, /37, /67–/74) are in route 1. Route 4: 'the cyclic and paracyclic categories, the cofinality of Δ^op → Λ_∞^op, and Bousfield–Kan homotopy colimits', but /148 and /150 are in route 1; route 4 carries /153, /157–/160. The verdicts are still defensible, but the reasons show that routes 2–4 were not checked item by item.
